summary: The formal-authority claim survives this bounded provenance challenge. Fourteen replay receipts match the source manifest and report stable source with exit zero; the audit output contains 66 root records. The manuscript correctly retains the inherited-object trust boundary. Canonical snapshot and manuscript hashes match. No clean dependency rebuild or independent reproduction was performed in this review.

checks.scope: Axiom-audit authority versus inherited compiled-object provenance
checks.method: Compared all fourteen F24 receipt source hashes against F01; inspected FrontierAudit.lean, its actual replay output, and F25 negative controls.
checks.observation: The auditor checks existence, theorem kind, proposition type, and transitive axiom allowlisting; controls record rejection of missing, non-theorem, and disallowed-axiom cases. These establish the claimed local audit behavior, not authenticity of inherited object bytes. F24 explicitly discloses reused A1K/mathlib objects, and the manuscript preserves that limitation instead of promoting source agreement into full rebuild assurance.
